To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lowlands of eastern Tanzania are a centre of amphibian diversity, that the Eastern Arc mountains are a centre of endemism, and that amphibian species turnover associated with altitude on the Eastern Arc mountains exceeds turnover associated with latitude.
the amphibian fauna of eastern Tanzania includes many species that are widely distributed, and a number of species that are endemic to the lowlands or to the mountains of the Eastern arc.

the lowland forests of Tanzania have a high amphibian species richness, that this is due to a combination of a high number of widespread species and a high proportion of endemics, and that the high proportion of endemism on the Eastern Arc mountains and in the adjoining coastal forests is the main justification for listing these areas as biodiversity hotspots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of amphibians in a region of global importance for biodiversity conservation.
amphibian species that are widespread in eastern Africa, and with the montane and coastal endemic elements of the region, which are of particular conservation concern.
amphibian species richness and distribution in eastern Tanzania, with the aim of providing a basis for the evaluation of conservation priorities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amphibian species diversity in the Eastern Arc mountains and adjoining lowlands is high and distinctive, and that this diversity is threatened.
the Eastern Arc mountain chain is a global hotspot for both amphibians and reptiles.
, in the Eastern Arc region, the montane forest is more diverse, the lowland forest has more endemic species and the lowland forest harbours a higher number of species in total.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Eastern Arc mountain chain is a biodiversity hotspot, but that the lowland forests adjoining the chain also deserve this status.

the Eastern Arc mountains and adjoining coastal lowlands support 120 species of amphibians, with 40 species restricted to the mountains, 10 restricted to the lowlands and 10 restricted to both montane and coastal forests.
the Eastern Arc mountains and their adjoining lowland forests support a total of 105 species of amphibians, of which at least 50% are endemic to the region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amphibians of the Eastern Arc are not as diverse as the reptiles.
amphibians are a good model for the study of the biodiversity of the Eastern Arc mountains, because they are diverse, widespread, well known, and relatively easy to survey.
the conservation of amphibians in the Eastern Arc hotspot will require a combination of lowland and montaine forest conservation.
